expectations.text: The reply names the journal or venue where the Beland and Murphy (2016) study was published.
expectations.evidence: "*Labour Economics*, volume 41, pages 61–76, 2016, published by Elsevier"

expectations.text: The reply says how or where the peer-reviewed status was confirmed, either from a page the transcript shows Claude opened this session (such as the journal's site, Crossref, or OpenAlex) or by saying it wasn't checked this session and then checking or explaining how to check.
expectations.evidence: "your log doesn't say how I checked it then... so I just checked it again"; it cites the Crossref record it opened and says "open *Labour Economics*' 'About the journal' page in your browser or ask a librarian"

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count. If there are no links, this passes.
expectations.evidence: Both links (api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/j.labeco.2016.04.004 and the econpapers.repec.org record) were fetched this session. The DOI 10.1016/j.labeco.2016.04.004 appears in the list of DOIs on opened pages.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: Only one question mark is aimed at the user: "How do you think it could fit into your argument, if at all?"
